title: No need to pay for ordinary, midday commutes, DOL says
summary: The agency addressed compensable working time in a pair of opinion letters Wednesday.

title: Electrician files harassment lawsuit against former employer, supervisor
summary: The plaintiff, who worked at the Hanford Vit Plant in Richland, Washington, allegedly faced repeated incidents of sexual harassment on the jobsite.

title: More than half of workers say they’ve considered accepting a lower offer after a layoff
summary: Glassdoor findings show a potential worsening of the gender pay gap through layoffs.

title: Labor Department proposes rule expanding disclosure e-delivery for employer plans
summary: The rule pitched Wednesday would make it easier for group health plans regulated by ERISA to share mandatory notices with their members. A DOL official called the proposal a “big step forward.”

title: What 10 leading restaurant companies pay their CEOs — and their hourly workers
summary: Median hourly compensation hovers near, and sometimes below, the poverty line, while leading restaurant CEOs earn tens of millions.

title: Workers who direct AI agents outperform peers who simply delegate to them
summary: Even when other skill sets were identical, the ability to judge artificial intelligence output made a critical difference in performance, per a study from KPMG and University of Texas at Austin.

title: 1 in 4 workers stay in unwanted jobs for health coverage, survey finds
summary: More Americans are keeping jobs they would otherwise leave for fear of losing their insurance, as healthcare costs rise and nonemployer coverage seems less affordable, according to a new poll.

title: Men use outside job offers to negotiate pay while women do not, per Swedish study
summary: Researchers recommended implementing structured wage-setting practices that reduce the role of bargaining in setting pay.

title: Federal HR office lost more than a third of its workforce during Trump’s second term, GAO reports
summary: The watchdog said the losses hampered “operational capacity” at the U.S. Office of Personnel Management and “risk worsening pre-existing skills gaps.”

title: The ‘average’ mind doesn’t exist: How work experts are thinking about neurodiversity
summary: HR may need to bridge the gap when it comes to their workforce’s empathy and understanding for neurodiverse workers.
